text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Malawi Posts and Telecommunications Corporation chief executive Steve Mijiga has been retired, a year after a controversial renewal of his contract, and replaced by his deputy Mike Makawa, board chair Fredson Mambiya said on Monday.

- Thousands of faithful thronged the streets of Blantyre, the main industrial city, on Monday as they converged at a Stadium to welcome German evangelist Reinhard Bonnke in the country at the start of what he called the "Great Gospel Crusade".

- The main opposition Malawi Congress Party vice-president Gwanda Chakuamba announced on Monday the party would hold its annual convention on June 30, in Lilongwe to decide whether or not to merge with another opposition Alliance for Democracy into one party and begin preparations for 1999 general elections.
- Malawi Army is struggling to settle a 12 million kwacha electricity bill it has owed for more than a year with Electricity Supply Commission (ESCOM).

- President Bakili Muluzi on Saturday at a rally cleared the police of accusations of corruption, contradicting inspector general Patrick Chikapa who admitted last week that there was corruption in the police force.
